ideas.risks: The candidate may only have proper or refutation hardness, not improper prediction hardness. The weak approximator may fail for arbitrary signed/weighted distribution-free instances, or the domain may become table-learnable/public-label trivial.
ideas.summary: Pick one concrete succinct-domain optimization class and test the full approximation-gap template end-to-end: define the query domain, keep the sign/RHS as the label, prove or cite a distribution-free signed/weighted constant-approximation algorithm giving fixed slack, and formulate strong-side RCN hardness at eta >= gamma against arbitrary evaluable improper predictors.
ideas.title: Instantiate Approximation-Gap Separation
ideas.why_promising: The solver attempt isolates the cleanest conditional negative template. A single fully checked candidate would turn the current vague route into either a serious conditional separation or a precise no-go checklist.

ideas.risks: The DCHP proof may genuinely need uniform control over exponentially many hidden-clean tuples, not just realized calls. The final selector and clean-population transfer bottlenecks may remain unchanged.
ideas.summary: Re-audit the da Cunha-Hogsgaard-Paudice proof with a strict separation between realized adaptive weak calls, hidden-clean population transfer, and final validation. Try to replace global Range(A)/dual-VC assumptions wherever possible using only realized-call union bounds and validation-independent finite lists of complete classifiers.
ideas.title: Realized-Call DCHP Extraction
ideas.why_promising: Some capacity assumptions may be proof artifacts for final selection or PAC-call validity. Removing even one global range assumption would sharpen the best positive conditional theorem.

ideas.risks: Actual DCHP query distributions may put too much mass on the programmed slices. Coupon/key accounting, confidence parameters, constants or offsets, extra generated columns, and T alignment may break the construction.
ideas.summary: Try to make rare-slice generated-bag pollution fully compatible with a DCHP-style bag generator. Specify key slices, stateful or stateless column scheduling, iid realization of hard rows, constants/offset columns, and show whether Set-Cover-hard sparse-majority bags can actually appear while each weak output remains OPT+beta valid.
ideas.title: DCHP Generated-Bag Pollution
ideas.why_promising: Generic sparse-majority ERM is hard only for arbitrary bags. This direction tests whether semantic weak correctness alone can also make generated bags selector-hard in black-box reductions.

ideas.risks: The resulting model may be too restricted to inform the atlas edge. Public witnesses, empirical spikes, other concepts, and hypothesis-handle leakage can make the invariant false or vacuous.
ideas.summary: Formalize a stopped-process oracle model with a random hidden target and clean mask. Route queries into target-preserving smooth filters, public-witness relabelings, empirical/spike queries, and other-concept witnesses. Prove that until a public low-posterior chunk appears, an adversarial weak oracle can answer canonically; charge the first low-posterior crossing by mutual information.
ideas.title: Stopped Public-Posterior Barrier
ideas.why_promising: The local posterior and KL lemmas are already clean. A stopped-process theorem would convert scattered obstructions into a reusable restricted black-box lower bound.

ideas.risks: If an efficient parity slice remains, the existing pullback lemma kills the construction under LPN. If no slice is sampleable, the weak learner may no longer be distribution-free or efficient.
ideas.summary: Explore whether the shrinking-gap parity near-separation can be transformed into a fixed-constant candidate only by genuinely non-sliceable amplification. Either construct a class where low-noise weak approximation is easy but hard-band RCN prediction hides parity, or prove a broader pullback theorem showing any plausible amplification exposes an efficiently sampleable parity slice.
ideas.title: Non-Sliceable Parity Amplification
ideas.why_promising: Parity is the sharpest known boundary example. Simple products, mixtures, and padding are blocked, so the remaining question is whether non-sliceability is a real escape or an illusion.

ideas.risks: The useful margin may exist only on hidden clean samples and not on observable noisy validation data. Worst-case Set-Cover hardness may persist under the promises that DCHP actually provides.
ideas.summary: Study the exact DCHP final class sign(B^(T)) under structured promises rather than arbitrary bags. Look for a polynomial selector using margin, anti-concentration, monotonicity, no-complement restrictions, or generated-bag structure; in parallel, try to adapt Set-Cover gadgets to survive those promises.
ideas.title: Promised Sparse-Majority Selector
ideas.why_promising: A universal selector is unavailable, but the positive route only needs selectors for generated or promised bags. This is a focused way to attack one key DCHP bottleneck.

ideas.risks: Arbitrary agnostic distributions need not provide repeated coordinates, independent noise, or observable clean bias. Validation can select complete classifiers but cannot validate useful intermediate weak hypotheses.
ideas.summary: Search for mechanisms that replace all-clean transcript enumeration by partially-clean denoising: repeated-coordinate majority, list-decoding from noisy tuples, disagreement-based localization, or class-specific robust reconstruction. State exact assumptions under which a polynomial noisy sample generates a validation-independent list containing a classifier good on D_c^+.
ideas.title: Partially-Clean Witness Generation
ideas.why_promising: The main positive bottleneck is total all-clean witness length. Any inverse-polynomial reconstruction from partially noisy evidence would bypass the p^K barrier in a meaningful conditional setting.

ideas.risks: Polynomial output length still permits large VC and rare-slice junk. Distribution-free validation cannot detect off-distribution behavior, so black-box canonicalization may be impossible without class-aware structure.
ideas.summary: Define a precise output/evaluation model for the supplied weak learner and investigate whether one can canonicalize it into a high-probability, query-relevant controlled-range learner. If not, strengthen rare-slice junk into a lower bound against validation-based pruning, quotienting, or syntactic compression.
ideas.title: Weak-Learner Canonicalization Model
ideas.why_promising: DCHP-style positive routes need controlled range or a substitute. The current rare-slice example refutes free global control, but a sharper model could identify exactly which natural regularization assumptions are sufficient or impossible.
